Original mini-fable: a fox knew every road on his map. Then the bridge moved.

我不知道。
Wǒ bù zhīdào.
I don’t know.

He feared those words would make him look foolish. Admitting uncertainty finally let him ask the way home.

Hana read 您 and wondered if “you” had changed.

您 nín — you, respectful
你 nǐ — you

Same listener, different form of address. 您 adds respect; one character alone can’t tell you whether a message is warm or distant. Context still matters.

Fictional scene: Hana rehearsed her speech. Then the microphone arrived early.

我还没准备好。
Wǒ hái méi zhǔnbèi hǎo.
I’m not ready yet.

还没 hái méi = not yet. The sentence she needed wasn’t the perfect speech. It was the one that bought a moment.

Original mini-fable: Rabbit declared the bridge impossible. Turtle tested one step.

我来试试。
Wǒ lái shìshi.
Let me try.

试试 shìshi = give it a try. Her answer promised an attempt, not success. One careful test taught her more than his speech.
